question: Should ClawHub accept publisher-follow notifications as an in-app private notification surface after the blocking visibility, fanout, proof, and stack issues are fixed?
rationale: The PR adds new durable private user notification state and publication fanout behavior, so implementation fixes alone do not settle the product/API boundary.

options.title: Accept after blockers and proof
options.body: Proceed only after the visibility gate, bounded fanout, dependency stack, and real runtime proof are resolved.

options.title: Review the stack together
options.body: Hold this PR until the base API and follow-controls PRs are ready so maintainers can judge the full follow feature at once.

options.title: Defer notification delivery
options.body: Land only the follow graph/discovery pieces and defer durable notification fanout to a later design pass.

recommendation.title: Accept after blockers and proof
recommendation.body: Proceed only after the visibility gate, bounded fanout, dependency stack, and real runtime proof are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: The most central current-main history for the publish paths, schema package, and retention policy points to this area owner signal.
